**Repaired finding submitted: Compliant (no redline).**

I closed the two residual points the verifier raised:

1. **§ 14 accounting-records reference (p0094–p0101, read in full).** The clause is a purely mutual *definition* plus six standard carve-outs (a)–(f). The phrase "accounting records for which access is obtained by the other party pursuant to this Agreement" describes the scope of Confidential Information and is *conditioned* on access obtained under some other provision — it grants no entry, examination or delivery right. § 1(b) merely cross-refers the definition to § 14. No operative provision anywhere supplies the access that § 14 presupposes.

2. **Schedules A–F.** They are incorporated by p0019 ("shall form an integral part of this Agreement") but appear in the text only as titles: Fee Schedule; Software and Documentation; Authorized Locations and Software copies; Specifications, Modifications, Data Conversion; Implementation and Training; Telephone Support. None is a reporting, certification or verification schedule, and no operative clause — including § 11, a bare obligation to pay Fee Schedule fees — imports any usage-reporting or true-up right from them.

Together with § 3 (substantive use limits only), § 20 (notices boilerplate) and § 17(b) (one-off post-termination self-certification of destruction/return, no vendor entry or system access), the conclusion holds: no audit right binds us, so the AUDIT parameters cannot arise. The failed "audit frequency limited" check reflects the absence of any audit clause, not a defective edit. No redline and no counterparty comment — adding audit machinery would create a Customer obligation and enlarge Garman's rights.
